# LaunchFree.io — The Runway

> LaunchFree.io (brand name: The Runway) is a free, human-reviewed launch directory for founders, indie makers, and side hustlers. Anyone can submit a product, service, business, or idea and receive a permanent listing page with a free dofollow backlink, a "Listed on The Runway" badge, and a feature in the weekly "Runway Radar" newsletter. Listing is free forever — no fees, no approval fee, no paywall — and every submission is reviewed by a real person within about 24 hours.

Operated by Automated Income Tools LLC. Founder: Julie James. Contact: hello@launchfree.io. There are currently 212 live launches spanning categories including AI / ML, Developer Tools, SaaS, Creator Tools, Productivity, Fintech, Education, Other, Health, Service, Marketing, Travel, Community, E-commerce, Affiliate, Entertainment, Lifestyle.

## Key pages
- [Home](https://launchfree.io/): What The Runway is and why it exists: a free, human-reviewed launch directory. Every launch needs a runway; yours is free.
- [Browse the Runway](https://launchfree.io/browse.html): The full, filterable grid of every live launch, searchable by category, stage, and popularity.
- [Directory (all launches, static HTML)](https://launchfree.io/directory.html): Every launch as plain links grouped by category — the full catalog, crawlable without JavaScript.
- [Submit your launch](https://launchfree.io/submit.html): Free submission form. After a ~24-hour human review you get a permanent listing page, a free dofollow backlink, a badge, and a newsletter feature.
- [Runway Radar](https://launchfree.io/radar.html): The content hub of free-launch guides — where to launch for free, how dofollow backlinks help SEO, and how to get traction with no audience or budget.
- [Bootstrap Founder Tools](https://launchfree.io/bootstrap-founder-tools.html): Guide and hub for bootstrapped founders looking to launch and get discovered for free.
- [Free Product Launch Directory](https://launchfree.io/free-product-launch-directory.html): Overview of LaunchFree as a genuinely free, no-paywall alternative to paid launch platforms.
- [Indie Maker Directory](https://launchfree.io/indie-maker-directory.html): Directory hub for indie makers and solo builders to list side projects and MVPs for free.
- [Launch Your SaaS Free](https://launchfree.io/launch-saas-free.html): How to launch a SaaS product for free on The Runway and earn a permanent dofollow backlink.
- [Privacy Policy](https://launchfree.io/privacy.html): How LaunchFree.io handles data and privacy.
- [Terms](https://launchfree.io/terms.html): Terms of use for LaunchFree.io.
- [Disclaimer](https://launchfree.io/disclaimer.html): Site disclaimer for LaunchFree.io.

## Runway Radar (guides)
- [Runway Radar](https://launchfree.io/radar.html): Honest, practical guides on launching for free: where to list, how to earn dofollow backlinks, and how to get traction with no audience or budget. From the team behind The Runway.
- [Where to Launch Your Product for Free in 2026 (No Pay-to-Win)](https://launchfree.io/radar/where-to-launch-your-product-for-free-2026.html): An honest, curated guide to the best free places to launch your product this year, organized by what you actually need: reach, early adopters, or a permanent backlink.
- [Do Directory Backlinks Still Help SEO in 2026?](https://launchfree.io/radar/do-directory-backlinks-help-seo.html): Short answer: yes, but only the right ones. Here's how directory backlinks actually move the needle, and how to tell a valuable listing from a waste of time.
- [Free vs. Pay-to-Win Launch Platforms: An Honest Breakdown](https://launchfree.io/radar/free-vs-pay-to-win-launch-platforms.html): Not every paid feature is a scam, and not every free platform is generous. Here's how to tell the difference, and when paying is actually worth it.
- [How to Launch a Product With No Audience or Budget](https://launchfree.io/radar/how-to-launch-with-no-audience-or-budget.html): No email list, no followers, no ad spend. You can still launch and get traction. Here's the honest, zero-dollar playbook.
- [Product Hunt Alternatives That Give You a Permanent Listing](https://launchfree.io/radar/product-hunt-alternatives-permanent-listing.html): Product Hunt's spotlight lasts a day. These alternatives give you something that lasts: a listing that keeps working for months.
- [The Best Free Startup Directories for Dofollow Backlinks (2026)](https://launchfree.io/radar/best-free-startup-directories-dofollow-backlinks.html): A shortlist of free directories that actually pass SEO value, plus how to submit efficiently without turning it into a second job.
- [The Best Launch Platforms for Indie Makers and Side Projects](https://launchfree.io/radar/launch-platforms-for-indie-makers.html): Big launch platforms can feel intimidating when it's just you and a side project. These are the friendlier places built for small, scrappy launches.
- [The Pre-Launch Website Checklist: 15 Things to Fix Before You List](https://launchfree.io/radar/pre-launch-website-checklist.html): Before you submit anywhere, spend an hour on these. They're the difference between a listing that converts and one people bounce from.
- [How to Get Your First 100 Users After Launch](https://launchfree.io/radar/how-to-get-your-first-100-users.html): Launch day gives you a spike. Here's how to turn it into your first hundred real users, and keep the momentum after the feed moves on.
- [What Makes a Good Product Launch Page (With a Simple Template)](https://launchfree.io/radar/what-makes-a-good-launch-page.html): A launch page has one job: turn a curious visitor into a user. Here's the simple structure that does it, and the mistakes that quietly kill conversions.
- [Show HN, Reddit, and Free Communities: A Launch-Day Playbook](https://launchfree.io/radar/show-hn-reddit-free-launch-communities.html): Community launches are free and powerful, and easy to get wrong. Here's how to launch on Hacker News, Reddit, and niche communities without getting flamed.
- [How Long Should Your Launch Last? The 24-Hour Myth](https://launchfree.io/radar/how-long-should-your-launch-last.html): Launch day culture says you get one shot in a 24-hour window. That's a platform's rule, not a law of nature. Here's how to think about launch timing instead.
- [SaaS, Digital Product, or Service: Where Each Should Launch](https://launchfree.io/radar/where-to-launch-saas-vs-digital-product-vs-service.html): The best place to launch depends on what you're launching. A quick guide to matching your product type to the right free channels.
- [The Founder's Guide to Launch-Day Copy That Converts](https://launchfree.io/radar/launch-day-copy-guide.html): The words you use on launch day decide whether people click or scroll. A practical guide to writing copy that sounds human and actually converts.
- [Free Newsletter Directories to Grow Your Launch's Audience](https://launchfree.io/radar/free-newsletter-directories-to-grow-your-audience.html): If your launch has a newsletter, listing it in the right directories is a quiet, free way to keep new subscribers trickling in long after launch day.
